speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your loss of consciousness, can you describe exactly what happened during the episode, such as any warning signs, movements, or how quickly you regained awareness? Also, have you experienced similar events in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That timing immediately after urination is highly suggestive of a specific reflex; did you experience any palpitations, chest pain, or a "racing heart" sensation just before you passed out? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, heart disease, or have you ever been told you have an enlarged prostate?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: ECG (Electrocardiogram) to check for bradycardia or heart block.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope (vasovagal syncope triggered by bladder emptying).
